content.overview: Vegetative cuttings reproduce the donor genotype while creating a new root system from stem tissue. Cutting quality, sanitation, hydration, rooting environment, genotype, and acclimatization all influence success.

vocabulary.definition: A donor plant maintained to supply vegetative cuttings.
A root that forms from tissue other than an existing root, such as a stem cutting.
The atmospheric and plant conditions driving water loss from leaves.
Gradual transition from protected propagation conditions into the normal growing environment.

sections.title: Donor quality sets the starting point
sections.body: Cuttings inherit the donor genotype and begin with the physiological condition of the selected shoot. Healthy, appropriately mature material provides a stronger starting point than stressed or diseased tissue.

sections.title: Fresh wounds increase sanitation importance
sections.body: Cutting tools and propagation surfaces can move pathogens into vulnerable tissue. Clean technique reduces one avoidable source of rooting failure.

sections.title: Unrooted cuttings have limited water replacement
sections.body: Before roots form, leaves can lose water faster than the cutting can replace it. Humidity, temperature, leaf area, and airflow should reduce excessive water loss without creating persistently stagnant conditions.

sections.title: Acclimatization reconnects roots and shoots
sections.body: Visible roots do not mean a cutting is ready for abrupt environmental exposure. The transition should progressively increase normal transpiration demand while the new root system expands.

workedExamples: If freshly rooted cuttings wilt immediately outside a dome, reduce the transition rate instead of assuming the roots are nonfunctional.
If one cultivar roots slower than another, track genotype-specific timing before making large environmental changes.
Cuttings remain turgid but show no roots by the expected batch window. The learner compares genotype, donor condition, temperature, media moisture and sanitation before increasing humidity further.
Rooted cuttings show severe wilt only after lights intensify. The acclimatization load likely increased faster than root water-supply capacity.
commonMistakes: Taking cuttings from obviously stressed donor tissue.
Keeping rooted cuttings indefinitely in extremely high humidity.
Assuming all cultivars root at the same rate.
Judging success only by leaf turgor before roots are confirmed.
Increasing humidity indefinitely instead of progressing acclimatization.
content.practicalApplication: Standardize donor selection, cutting size, sanitation, media, environmental conditions, rooting checks, and acclimatization steps. Track results by genotype and batch so improvements are based on evidence.
content.summary: Cloning is controlled regeneration of a new root system from donor tissue. Healthy donors, sanitation, water-loss management, genotype-aware rooting, and gradual acclimatization make the process more repeatable.

blocks.title: A cutting must survive before it can root
blocks.body: Detached shoots continue losing water through leaves while lacking a functional root system. Propagation conditions reduce transpirational demand long enough for wound responses and adventitious roots to develop.

blocks.title: Cloning checkpoints
rows: Maintains turgor under progressively normal conditions

blocks.title: Run a clone batch as a controlled process

items.title: Select healthy donors
items.body: Avoid symptomatic or weak source tissue.

items.title: Standardize cuts
items.body: Use clean tools and consistent cutting dimensions.

items.title: Manage water loss
items.body: Balance humidity, temperature, leaf area and airflow.

items.title: Compare batch outcomes
items.body: Change one major variable at a time.

blocks.title: Rooted but not ready
blocks.setting: Cuttings have short new roots but wilt as soon as the dome is fully removed.
options: Acclimatization is too abrupt for current root capacity
blocks.answer: Acclimatization is too abrupt for current root capacity.
blocks.feedback: Root presence does not guarantee the plant can immediately support normal transpiration demand.

blocks.title: Clone batch performance review
prompts: Identify whether failure occurs before or after root formation.
Choose one protocol variable to test next.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: Cloning success includes survival, root formation and successful acclimatization—not visible roots alone.
